timeline.event: The Spanish found St. Augustine in Florida
English colonists found Jamestown in Virginia
The Mayflower Pilgrims found Plymouth Colony
Colonists dump British tea into Boston Harbor
The Declaration of Independence is adopted
The U.S. Constitution is signed in Philadelphia
The Louisiana Purchase doubles the nation's size
The Erie Canal opens, linking the Great Lakes to the Atlantic
Gold is found at Sutter's Mill, sparking the California Gold Rush
The Civil War begins with the attack on Fort Sumter
The first transcontinental railroad is completed
The Wright brothers make the first powered airplane flight
The Nineteenth Amendment grants women the right to vote
Wall Street crashes, ushering in the Great Depression
Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
The Supreme Court rules on Brown v. Board of Education
Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon
Terrorist attacks destroy the World Trade Center's Twin Towers

places.name: Washington, D.C.
places.clue: The capital's grand avenues and diagonal streets were planned by French-born engineer Pierre L'Enfant in 1791.

places.name: Statue of Liberty
places.clue: A gift from France dedicated in 1886, its copper skin has slowly weathered to its famous green.

places.name: Grand Canyon
places.clue: The Colorado River carved this gorge over 1.8 km deep, exposing rocks nearly two billion years old at its bottom.

places.name: Golden Gate Bridge
places.clue: When it opened in 1937, its 1,280 m main span was the longest of any suspension bridge in the world.

places.name: Yellowstone National Park
places.clue: Established in 1872, it is widely regarded as the world's first national park and holds about half of Earth's geysers.

places.name: New Orleans
places.clue: Founded by the French in 1718 near the mouth of the Mississippi, it is celebrated as the birthplace of jazz.

places.name: Mount Rushmore
places.clue: Each of the four presidents' faces carved into its granite stands about 18 m tall.

places.name: The Alamo
places.clue: In 1836 a small garrison held this former Spanish mission for 13 days before it fell to Mexican forces.

places.name: Everglades
places.clue: Nicknamed the 'River of Grass', this vast wetland is a rare place where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.

places.name: Cahokia Mounds
places.clue: Its Monks Mound is the largest prehistoric earthwork in the Americas, raised by Mississippian people about a thousand years ago.

places.name: Mesa Verde
places.clue: Ancestral Puebloans tucked the Cliff Palace, with around 150 rooms, into a sandstone alcove here.

places.name: Crater Lake
places.clue: Filling the collapsed crater of an ancient volcano, it is the deepest lake in the country at about 594 m.
